layoutReference.inspection: Actual pixels inspected: opposed left/right face and body directions, 24 studies, four rows of six. No species/anatomy/clothing transfer.

bear.speciesAndRole: Adult brown bear builder, olive canvas apron; Papa adult hedgehog; Beaver adult blue-vest beaver.
bear.designBasis: Established R17 adaptation study and published art; 1.35 Papa height is a study proposal, not original fact.

talking-duck.speciesAndRole: Magically sentient small yellow rubber bath duck with orange bill and molded wings; PinPin child hedgehog, Papa/Mama adult hedgehogs.
talking-duck.designBasis: Published talking duck appearance; distinct sentient individual, not generic incidental ducks.

tutu.speciesAndRole: Female squirrel friend Tutu; PinPin child hedgehog, Rabbit/Lulu rabbit peer.
tutu.designBasis: Original chapter9 establishes female squirrel friend with nut basket. Original chapter4 group image supplies squirrel silhouettes but no identified Tutu portrait. Russet fur, cream belly, tufted ears and fluffy curved tail are proposed current adaptation details.

pipilini.speciesAndRole: Older male migrating bird Pipilini/Pipilino with weak wings; PinPin child hedgehog, Mama/Papa adult hedgehogs.
pipilini.designBasis: Original chapter8 old migrating bird, weak wings, invited winter guest. Original image49 contains a pale rose long-tailed bird with reddish bill but does not uniquely label it. Rose/cream bird adaptation is an explicitly proposed visual interpretation; species and exact age not stated.

mama-beaver.speciesAndRole: Adult female beaver mother, red scarf, smooth fur and paddle tail
mama-beaver.designBasis: Published Beaver family scenes321/334; preserve finished corrected art.

beaver-kits.speciesAndRole: Two young beaver kits, separate bodies, paddle tails; names/sex/exact ages not stated
beaver-kits.designBasis: Published Beaver family scenes321/334; preserve finished corrected art.

oreshek.speciesAndRole: Old male gray squirrel elder. Gray fur is explicit original chapter19 block4. Proposed warm adaptation: cream muzzle/belly, gently weathered brows, tufted ears and bushy gray curved tail, no clothing. NOT a hedgehog.
oreshek.designBasis: Original group image shows gray squirrel among digging animals but does not label Oreshek; individual face and proportions are proposed.

lilia.speciesAndRole: Elderly female squirrel forest wizard, HUGE round glass spectacles; original chapter30 blocks3–7 and chapter31 block2. Proposed warm adaptation: muted russet silver-tipped fur, cream face/belly, fluffy silver-gray curved tail. No wizard hat or human body.
lilia.designBasis: Original magical squirrel image provides scene context but lacks the text-required spectacles and does not prove a named portrait. Spectacles/elderly female squirrel are textual facts; adapted facial design proposed.

hedgehog-cousins.speciesAndRole: Young unnamed hedgehog cousins. Source establishes a group, no exact total, names, sex or ages. Show TWO representative proposed designs, not a claim of canonical count: A warm tawny quills, B cooler brown quills; both cream muzzle/belly, small rounded ears, compact young child proportions, no clothing. Both are walking children, not infants.
hedgehog-cousins.designBasis: Original breakfast group contains many young hedgehogs with varied sizes; no individual names or count established. Two representative adaptations are proposals.

spring-birds.speciesAndRole: Exactly two small published spring birds: orange-breasted brown-backed robin-like bird and blue-capped blue-winged yellow-bellied tit-like bird with white cheeks/dark eye stripe. Preserve published colors, short beaks, two wings/two feet/tail each; no mammal arms. Species resemblance is visual inference, not taxonomic canon.
spring-birds.designBasis: Published scene04d explicitly names two little birds and pixels establish two distinct feather patterns and size relative to PinPin. Exact ages and names not stated.

squirrel-community.speciesAndRole: Recurring unnamed squirrel community: experienced adult advisers/builders and their young are sourced. Show TWO representative proposed designs, not canonical total: one older gray-brown adviser with cream muzzle and one smaller russet youngster with cream belly; tufted ears, bushy tails, squirrel paws, no hedgehog quills. No personal names or precise ages, no inferred sex. Adults capable of planning/building; young age-appropriate play.
squirrel-community.designBasis: Original chapters19–25 establish advisers, builders and young, with actual image73 showing varied squirrels working with hedgehogs. Group visuals establish diversity, not named individual portraits. Two representative faces/colors/relative sizes are proposed book adaptations.

migrating-bird-family.speciesAndRole: Recurring unnamed bird family migrates south to Africa each year; old Pipilini used to lead the flock but cannot travel that far now (original chapter8). Show TWO representative capable flying birds, mature-looking larger and smaller companion, not canonical count, sex or asserted parent/chick relationship. Proposed pale rose/cream feather design related to working Pipilini with reddish small beaks, folded feather wings, thin supported feet, long light rose tails. No mammal arms. Pipilini is the separate older weak-winged character, not one of these active flying representatives.
migrating-bird-family.designBasis: Original chapter8 block3 establishes family and migration; relative ages within the family, number, species and individual appearance are not specified. Image49 has one unlabeled pale rose bird, not a family portrait. Proposed representative size/role differentiation remains explicitly unsourced; established older Pipilini identity is retained only as counterpart.

tarin.speciesAndRole: Tarin is a HUMAN WIZARD who deliberately took hedgehog form, returns to tall human form after enchanted coffee, then becomes hedgehog again at sunset (original chapter13 blocks6–10,12). HUMAN: old-looking male wizard, white wavy shoulder-length hair, long white beard and bushy brows, rounded pink nose, small round spectacles, rich gold robe with subtle embroidered trim and brown shoes, actual original image77 identity. HEDGEHOG: proposed elderly salt-and-pepper/gray-brown quills, cream face/chest, white eyebrows and warm brown eyes echoing human form, rounded ears/muzzle, natural two paws/two feet, no human beard or robe. Both depictions are ONE person in alternative forms, never two independent cast members.
tarin.designBasis: Human/hedgehog transformation is explicit source text. Actual original images77/71 show human wizard in gold robe with white beard/hair; glasses appear in77, not71. These control proposed dimensional human adaptation. No verified Tarin hedgehog portrait: hedgehog pictured beside wizard is a companion, not assumed Tarin. Tarin’s relationship to published hedgehog Elder is unresolved; keep this distinct requirement, do not copy or silently alias published Elder. The final human study retains a generated carved walking staff as a proposed prop, absent from inspected original portraits; it is not asserted as manuscript canon.
